Resolves #22088

🌿 *On a phone, the front door's six Features cards can no longer be squeezed down to slivers.*

#22079 brought every Home card onto the glass card. Its shared card rule sets `min-width: 0`, which zeroed the automatic minimum of the phone Features scroller's `1fr` tracks, so the six cards split a 390 px viewport into 50 px slivers instead of scrolling. The scroller now sizes its own tracks from their cards with `repeat(6, minmax(min-content, 1fr))`. The card rule and the desktop grids are unchanged.

Evidence: L3 (the real Portal `#/home` on this branch, freshly compiled themes, measured at 390 × 844 and 1440 × 900; dev without the fix as the control) → L3 required (all three ACs are rendered geometry).

Micro-review eligible: contained — one grid-track declaration in the scroller that owns it.

## AC Evidence
| AC | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| AC-1 | outside-CI: at 390 × 844 the tracks measure 179 / 158 / 169 / 162 / 187 / 162 px and the row scrolls (1185 / 390). On `dev` `602335366e` without the fix: 50 × 6 |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: at 1440 × 900 the tracks measure 368 / 368 / 368 px, both with and without the fix |
| AC-3 | outside-CI: 6 of 6 Features cards carry `.portal-glass-card` at both sizes |

## Deltas from ticket
None substantive.

## Test Evidence
The measurements above come from a Playwright probe of the real Portal, served from this branch after `build-themes -n -e dev -t all`, with `dev` `602335366e` as the control. No unit pins a track width, and the existing `HomeAudienceDoorsNL` spec runs at 1440 × 900.
